skills.description: use this when a newly imported Song Meter / BirdNET bot starts its first conversation with its owner and needs paths, regional list, schedule, and report style

---
name: song-meter-getting-started
description: >-
  use this when a newly imported Song Meter / BirdNET bot starts its first
  conversation with its owner and needs paths, regional list, schedule, and
  report style
---
# Song Meter / BirdNET — first conversation

You help the owner process Wildlife Acoustics Song Meter (Micro 2 or similar) SD cards with a local BirdNET CLI on their computer, then deliver short digests and optional PDF reports. The owner owns the hardware and files every claim of what was heard.

## What you do
Copy WAVs off the SD card onto their computer (off cloud sync), run BirdNET-Analyzer locally (CSV + Raven selection tables; no Raven GUI in chat), write summaries/reports with **Confident migration IN/OUT vs the prior card**, archive audio to an external drive, and free the working copy. Support Bluetooth mid-checks and field swaps via the dedicated skills. Never ship WAVs through chat or onto the box.

## Ask one at a time
1. What should I call you, and what timezone should I use?
2. Where should the **working audio** folder live on this computer? (example: `~/birding/cards/` — keep multi‑GB WAVs off cloud sync.)
3. Where should **scripts, species lists, run CSVs, Raven tables, and PDF reports** live? (any folder they choose — store the path, don’t assume a brand.)
4. Where is the **BirdNET venv** (or should I create `~/.venvs/birding`)?
5. Recorder model, unit name/serial, sample rate, and typical schedule (e.g. 05:00–22:00 with 30/30 duty, or 24/7).
6. Site label for reports (place name is enough; exact street address optional).
7. **Regional bird list** (critical) — see recipe below.
8. Archive volume path when they plug in a backup drive (example: `/Volumes/BIRDING/cards/`).
9. **Report style** (adjustable): confirm preferences before locking — title wording, Confident vs Possible (or high/medium/low), phenology, **migration vs prior card** (default on once a prior card exists), files column, TOC, OTHER CRITTERS / scout-reject appendix, night/owl timing in the chat digest. Start from sensible defaults only after they confirm or say “use defaults.”
10. Battery chemistry (lithium vs alkaline), planned mid-check and swap cadence, who owns calendar reminders?

## Regional list recipe (teach this, don’t assume a file exists)
Prefer a curated regional list over the full global list. **Do not use Cornell `--lat/--lon/--week` by default:** week filters routinely omit real local taxa (owls, nightjars, eagles, scarce breeders); some “year-round” / large lists also leak Old World taxa that pollute rankings. Curated lists usually work better **without** location/week filters.

If building from scratch:
1. Ask region (state/province or ecoregion).
2. Start from a regional bird checklist source they trust (or export from BirdNET’s taxonomy filtered to that region).
3. Ask which **extras** to force-include even if sparse on checklists: owls, raptors, shorebirds, nightjars, other locally important groups.
4. Ask **exclusions**: Old World leaks, pets, machinery/engine labels, insects if they want those out of the bird list.
5. Write a plain-text list BirdNET can load (one scientific or common name per line, matching the analyzer’s taxonomy). Save under their scripts/lists folder; remember the path.
6. After the first card: open-scout at ≥0.80 → propose misses → auto-add only taxa plausible for their region → reject insects/dog/engine/Old World → **rerun** the regional list after accepted adds.

## Battery / life estimates
- Micro 2 at 24 kHz **continuous 24/7** on 4 AA lithiums is about ~12 days (~283 h), not 1–2 months. A multi-week swap estimate fits **duty-cycled** daytime schedules, not continuous.
- The Song Meter app “Estimate battery and card life” assumes **alkaline** — treat it as a conservative underestimate for lithium.
- Lithium voltage often stays high then **cliffs**. Do **not** redeploy a pack that already cliffed even if it still reads ~6–7 V after recovery. Prefer fresh cells at each full swap.

## After answers
Write durable memories for timezone, paths, hardware, schedule, **regional list path + how it was built**, archive volume, report conventions, and battery rules. Remind them once that analysis waits until they say the card is in the computer. Offer Bluetooth mid-check and field-swap guidance, and a swap/mid-check reminder routine when they pick dates.

skills.name: song-meter-card-process
skills.description: use this when the owner says a Song Meter SD card is in the computer and wants copy, BirdNET, digest, report, and archive — including regional-list curation and migration vs prior card
skills.content:
---
name: song-meter-card-process
description: >-
  use this when the owner says a Song Meter SD card is in the computer and wants
  copy, BirdNET, digest, report, and archive — including regional-list curation
  and migration vs prior card
---
# Process one Song Meter card

## Token guard
Never CopyToBox audio, never attach WAVs to chat, never dump huge CSVs into context. Summarize with local scripts. Local BirdNET CPU time is fine. Write **Raven selection tables** beside run CSVs for offline review; do **not** drive Raven GUIs unless the owner asks.

## Before analysis
Confirm the **regional species list** path exists. If missing or they’re new: pause and help build/curate one using the regional-list recipe (region base → extras like owls/raptors/shorebirds/nightjars → exclusions → save path). Do not silently fall back to a full global list. **Do not pass `--lat/--lon/--week` unless they opted in** — week filters omit locals; some large lists leak Old World taxa.

## Pipeline
1. Find the SD volume on their computer; inventory WAVs (count, size, first/last timestamps). Skip tiny startup junk and truncated last files.
2. Copy WAVs into the working audio folder under a session id (`unit_YYYYMMDD-YYYYMMDD/`). Do not put multi‑GB dumps in cloud sync.
3. Dual BirdNET: open scout first, then the owner’s regional list (no lat/lon/week unless opted in). Min confidence typically 0.25 for ranking. Write CSV **and** Raven selection tables under their scripts/runs folder.
4. High-conf (≥0.80) scout misses: propose them; auto-add only taxa plausible for their region (update the list when they agree); reject insects, dog, engine, and clear Old World misIDs. Remap common owl mixups to local owls when that is their convention. **Rerun** the regional list after accepted adds. Scout rejects belong in an appendix, not the published species totals.
5. Build a **this-card-only** report using **their saved report preferences** (ask once if never set). Sensible defaults if they said “use defaults”: title “Passive Acoustic Monitoring Report”; site label on cover; Confident vs Possible bins; no TOC; no files column; OTHER CRITTERS / scout-reject appendix OK; skip long phenology until many months of data.
6. **Migration compare (first-class):** when a prior card’s published Confident set exists, compute Confident **IN / OUT** vs that card. Flag thin or noisy INs (single weak hits, clear non-local labels) for review in the digest. Include this in the PDF and chat digest unless they opted out.
7. Chat digest: card ID · date range · file count; detection/species totals and min conf; Top species with counts and max conf; less-common / worth-a-look; **migration IN/OUT**; night/owl timing if they want it. No CSV dump in chat.
8. Save the PDF under their reports folder (and Desktop only if they asked). When the archive drive is mounted, copy WAVs + PDF there, verify counts, then delete the working copy.
9. Do not reconfigure the recorder while it is deployed in the field. Field swap / Bluetooth mid-check use their dedicated skills.

## Report back
Concrete paths (including Raven tables), counts, digest highlights, migration IN/OUT, any list updates proposed/applied, archive status, and blockers (missing volume, missing regional list, BirdNET errors).

skills.description: use this when the owner does a Song Meter Bluetooth mid-check in the field (voltage, schedule, card fill, clock drift) without changing config

---
name: song-meter-bluetooth-midcheck
description: >-
  use this when the owner does a Song Meter Bluetooth mid-check in the field
  (voltage, schedule, card fill, clock drift) without changing config
---
# Song Meter Bluetooth mid-check

Use when the owner is near the deployed recorder and can open the Song Meter mobile app / Bluetooth status screen. **Do not change schedule, gain, sample rate, or other config while the unit is mid-deploy** unless they explicitly ask to abort the current session.

## Collect
Ask them to read (or screenshot) and report:
- Battery voltage (V)
- Schedule name / next recording time
- Recording count and used / total card space (GB and %)
- Firmware version if shown
- Whether the recorder clock matches the phone (note minutes of drift)

## Interpret
- Healthy mid-deploy: voltage still in a normal lithium plateau for their chemistry, schedule matches the planned block, card not nearly full before the planned swap.
- Clock drift of a couple of minutes: note it; **resync by PAIR at the next card/battery swap**, not mid-deploy, unless drift is severe and they want a deliberate stop.
- Red Bluetooth flash after a battery pull means the clock is unset — that is a **swap** situation (see field-swap skill), not a casual mid-check.

## Report back
A short status line: V · schedule / next rec · files · GB/% · firmware · clock drift · healthy or watch. Suggest next mid-check or swap window from their standing cadence. Offer to park a reminder routine if they want one.

skills.description: use this when the owner is at the Song Meter for a card and/or battery swap — Configurator Time-block schedule, PAIR after battery pull, fresh cells, empty card

---
name: song-meter-field-swap
description: >-
  use this when the owner is at the Song Meter for a card and/or battery swap —
  Configurator Time-block schedule, PAIR after battery pull, fresh cells, empty
  card
---
# Song Meter field swap (card + batteries)

Use when the owner is at the recorder to pull the SD card and/or replace batteries. Analysis of the pulled card is a separate card-process run after they say the card is in the computer.

## Safety
Do not reconfigure a unit that is still mid-deploy and supposed to keep recording. Swap = intentional stop/start of a session.

## Checklist
1. Note voltage before opening if they already peeked via Bluetooth.
2. Pull the SD card for copy/BirdNET later; leave a **fresh empty** card if they run dual cards or a wiped spare.
3. Install **fresh** cells. Prefer new lithiums after a cliff — do **not** redeploy a pack that already voltage-cliffed even if it still reads high.
4. After a battery pull, a **red Bluetooth flash** means the clock is unset: **PAIR** until green and set clock, timezone, and location from the phone at the site.
5. Confirm or set schedule in Song Meter Configurator / app:
   - Prefer one **Time** block (not Rise/Set, not a generic day-duty preset) when they want fixed clock hours.
   - Example pattern: START 05:00, Duty On 00:30 / Duty Off 00:30, END 22:00 (quiet nights) — use **their** chosen hours.
   - Leave sample rate, max file length, and gain as previously agreed (common Micro 2: 24 kHz, 60 min max file, gain 18 dB) unless they ask to change.
   - Bluetooth beacons On if they use mid-checks.
6. Confirm Custom Schedule (or their chosen mode) is active and the next recording time looks right.
7. Reminder: the app “Estimate battery and card life” assumes **alkaline** — lithium usually lasts longer than that estimate.

## After swap
Record deploy start, chemistry, schedule, and next mid-check / swap targets in memory. Offer a reminder routine. Tell them to say when the pulled card is in the computer so card-process can run.
